editorial.brief: Lizzie Borden topped Wikipedia with 1,022,634 views, nearly four times runner-up Resident Evil, with a Lifetime-style Monster series about her riding shotgun in fourth place. Nothing else crossed feeds today — Hacker News argued over AI papers, Lemmy stayed wry, and CS2 pulled 1.2 million concurrent players on Steam. A quiet news day with one clear obsession.
editorial.cover_sub: A 19th-century axe murder outdrew a 2026 horror film, a UFC card and a college football coach, carried by a same-named streaming dramatization sitting three slots behind it.
editorial.wiki_deck: A trial that ended in 1893 still beats the box office. The lead-over-second margin ran 3.8 times, driven by a dramatization of the same case two spots down the list.
editorial.letter_headline: One story, told twice, beats the field
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is deep in AI model papers and a Sun-era retrospective; Lemmy is wry and low-stakes; Bluesky is fixated on press-freedom lawsuits and gambling ads; Mastodon is split between AI-bubble jokes and a White House broadcasting gripe.
editorial.foreign_deck: The AI wire covered Oracle's near-maxed-out chip fleet and Anthropic's CEO urging a slower pace, while searches ranged from Brazilian and German gates to Japanese McDonald's menus and the US Powerball.
editorial.markets_deck: Today's top markets mix a long-shot 2028 presidential bet, a near-certain tennis result, a coin-flip Fed rate call, and a soccer title nobody expects Shakhtar to win — volume stayed thin throughout.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 held 1,218,401 concurrent Steam players, caseoh_ led Twitch with 59,016 viewers, and the Cliff Booth Netflix trailer pulled 3,801,819 YouTube views, well clear of anything else trending.
editorial.yt_headline: A Netflix trailer, not a game
editorial.yt_note: The trending list split evenly between a film trailer, two music videos, a horror-game playthrough and a streaming-show recap, with the Cliff Booth trailer clearing every other entry by several million views.
editorial.closing_note: Lizzie Borden's landslide will fade once the Monster series stops trending alongside her. UFC 331 and Lane Kiffin belong to news cycles that move on by Wednesday. The quakes, the thin markets, the zero-download model — none of it was built to last past today's edition.
wiki_paras: Lizzie Borden pulled 1,022,634 Wikipedia views today, more than the next four articles combined. Resident Evil (2026 film) came second at 268,382, followed immediately by Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story at 253,570 — the same case, dramatized, sitting two places behind the woman herself.

The margin was 3.8 times the runner-up, a gap wide enough to call a landslide by any newsroom's standards. The explanation sits in plain sight: a title with her name on it is charting alongside her, which is about as direct as cause and effect gets in a pageview chart.

UFC 331 and Lane Kiffin filled out the top five, sport doing what sport does on a Tuesday. But today belonged to an 1892 double murder in Fall River, Massachusetts, proof that a well-timed streaming title can still send a 133-year-old cold case back to the top of the internet.
letter_paras: Today's snapshot found no topic spanning multiple feeds — the cross-source tracker came back empty. Instead it found one very large single story sitting entirely inside Wikipedia: Lizzie Borden's page absorbing four times the traffic of anything else, with a dramatization of her case riding along two spots below. Everywhere else, the day was seventeen separate rooms talking past each other.
